culture.name: Dominican Republic
culture.timeDifference: It is the same time there or a few hours later, depending on where you live.
culture.homeTravelNote: a direct flight of a few hours from the East Coast

cookLines: Yuca, plantain and auyama go into the big pot, and the whole apartment smells like a Sunday at home.
You taste the sancocho and squeeze in a little more sour orange, the way your grandmother would.
{roommate} wanders in and asks what smells so good.
You ladle it over white rice with slices of avocado, and for an hour the kitchen is loud and warm.

festivals.title: Nochebuena
festivals.body: At home, Christmas Eve means roast pork, moro de guandules, merengue from every house on the street and family staying up past midnight. Campus is quiet and cold.
festivals.join: Spend the evening with a Dominican family nearby.
festivals.joinText: Their tía fills your plate twice before you sit down. Someone pushes the chairs back and the dancing starts.
festivals.host: Cook Nochebuena dinner for whoever is still on campus.
festivals.hostText: The pork takes all day and the oven is too small, and it comes out well anyway. Your friends learn the first steps of merengue in the hallway.
festivals.skip: Video-call the family dinner and go to bed early.
festivals.skipText: Your cousins pass the phone around the table so everyone can shout hello. You fall asleep to the sound of home.

festivals.title: Independence Day, 27 February
festivals.body: At home, February is carnival season, and the 27th closes it with parades, masks and flags in red, white and blue. Here it is a cold weekday in the middle of the semester.
festivals.join: Go to the Dominican students' Independence celebration.
festivals.joinText: Flags on every wall, a table of pastelitos and habichuelas con dulce, and a playlist that will not let anyone sit down. You dance until the room closes.
festivals.host: Cook for friends and put a small flag on the table.
festivals.hostText: Your friends try mangú for the first time and ask for more. You show them carnival videos from La Vega and they cannot believe the masks.
festivals.skip: Send greetings to the family chat and get back to work.
festivals.skipText: Your phone fills with photos of costumes and flags. You smile at every one.

festivals.title: Día de las Madres
festivals.body: At home, Mother's Day falls on the last Sunday of May, weeks after the American one, and the whole family gathers around mothers and grandmothers. Finals have just ended.
festivals.join: Join friends from the association for a Mother's Day brunch call.
festivals.joinText: Six laptops, six mothers on screen and everyone talking at once. Yours tells the whole group you are too thin.
festivals.host: Cook your mother's recipe and call her from the kitchen.
festivals.hostText: She watches you from the phone and corrects the seasoning from a whole sea away. When you finish, she says it looks almost right.
festivals.skip: Send flowers and call in the evening.
festivals.skipText: She holds the bouquet up to the camera and pretends not to cry. You promise to be there next year.

familyCall: Santo Domingo is level with the East Coast in summer and an hour ahead in winter, so your mother calls right after dinner.
She asks whether you are eating real food and whether you are wearing enough layers.
Your grandmother takes the phone to give you her blessing, and somewhere behind her the radio is playing bachata.
You hang up missing the noise of the house, and a little lighter.
culture.homeMoneyNote: Money from home is converted from Dominican pesos, so every transfer loses a little to fees and the exchange rate.
culture.familySupportNote: Designed value, kept at the India baseline of 1.0. This research found no sourced figure that would justify more or less family support for Dominican students, so it is left neutral.

entryNotes.F1: About 1,582 Dominicans studied in the US in 2024/25, and Dominican nationals received 1,255 F-1 visas in FY2024.
entryNotes.H1B: TN status is only for Canadian and Mexican citizens, so Dominican professionals need an H-1B or another work visa; the Dominican Republic is charged to the Rest of World green card queue.
entryNotes.B2: The Dominican Republic is not in the Visa Waiver Program, so visitors need a B visa from a US consulate before travelling.
entryNotes.O1: O-1 status needs a petition approved by USCIS and then a visa interview at a US consulate.
entryNotes.FAM: The Dominican Republic is not eligible for the Diversity Visa lottery, and it is not Dominica, the separate country named in the 2026 entry proclamation.
entryNotes.EWI: CBP does not report border encounters of Dominican nationals separately, and entering without inspection usually blocks a green card from inside the US later.
entryNotes.ASY: In FY2024 immigration courts granted 25 and denied 216 asylum cases from Dominican nationals, about 10 percent of decisions.

facts.title: Time difference to Santo Domingo
facts.text: Santo Domingo is on Atlantic Standard Time, UTC-4, all year with no daylight saving time. It is 1 hour ahead of US Eastern in winter and level with it in summer, and 4 hours ahead of Pacific in winter and 3 in summer.

facts.title: Round-trip flight, the Dominican Republic to US
facts.text: Design estimate of $500. No sourced fare range for the Dominican Republic to US round trips was found; real fares vary widely by route and season.

facts.title: F-1 visas issued to Dominicans
facts.text: Dominican nationals received 1,255 F-1 visas in FY2024, down from 1,394 in FY2023 and 1,513 in FY2022, and 1,240 in FY2025. Figures are State Department data republished by VisaGrader.

facts.title: Dominican students in the US
facts.text: 1,582 students from the Dominican Republic studied in the US in 2024/25, up from 1,542 the year before. The country ranked 64th among places of origin (Open Doors 2025).

facts.title: Remittances to the Dominican Republic
facts.text: The Dominican Republic received $11.87 billion in remittances in 2025, a record and about 10.3 percent more than in 2024. In December 2025 about 80 percent came from the United States (Banco Central de la República Dominicana, as reported).

facts.title: Asylum decisions for Dominican applicants
facts.text: In FY2024 immigration courts granted 25 and denied 216 asylum cases from Dominican nationals, about 10 percent of decisions. Another 213 were not adjudicated and 114 were abandoned. The numbers are small, and individual claims matter more than averages.

facts.title: Family green card queue for the Dominican Republic
facts.text: The Dominican Republic is charged to the Rest of World queue. November 2026 Visa Bulletin final action dates, as transcribed by a law firm: adult children of citizens (F1) 22 Jan 2021, married children (F3) 22 Oct 2015, siblings (F4) 22 Oct 2012. A sibling petition filed today faces a wait of roughly 14 years.

mechanics.asylumNote: FY2024 EOIR Asylum Decisions by Nationality: 25 grants and 216 denials (10.4 percent); 114 abandoned, 213 not adjudicated, 52 withdrawn. Small numbers. https://www.justice.gov/eoir/media/1344846/dl
